decision.winner_name: Drive Bardolino → Peschiera del Garda station → direct train to Venezia Santa Lucia
decision.rationale: This is the lowest-stress infant day that still reaches the real Venice (Santa Lucia, not Mestre). The car is parked once, in a normal station town 20 minutes from the apartment, instead of after 90–120 minutes of A4/lagoon traffic. Regional and Frecciarossa trains both run this corridor in about 1h28–1h50; infants ride free on regional services and are straightforward on high-speed with a reservation. You arrive already in the historic city, not in a garage on Tronchetto. The stroller stays folded; the baby lives in a carrier on the 400 stepped bridges. Organized Garda–Venice coaches were rejected because they steal nap control and often return after this family's 18:00 curfew. Driving to Piazzale Roma or Tronchetto was rejected because it maximizes time in a car seat, adds lagoon congestion, expensive garages, and a vaporetto transfer before the day even starts.

rejected_reasons.A: Longer baby-in-car-seat time, lagoon traffic, ZTL camera risk if you miss a sign, €21–45 garages, then still a vaporetto or People Mover. Stress peaks at the exact moment you wanted to be calm.
rejected_reasons.B: Mestre parking is cheaper, but you add a second urban layer (garage → Mestre station → train) for almost no gain versus parking at Peschiera, which you already pass geographically. Peschiera is the family's lake-side station; Mestre is a mainland city they do not need to learn.
rejected_reasons.D: Coach tours from the lake are rigid, often include Murano glass shops, pack the return, and frequently land back after 18:00. A six-month-old cannot vote to leave early.

modes.name: Drive to Tronchetto or Piazzale Roma
modes.notes: Piazzale Roma garages ~€35–45/24h, closest. Tronchetto ~€21–30, more space, People Mover or vaporetto after. Historic Venice is a ZTL. Peak A4 + Padova/Mestre beltway can blow the 18:00 return.

modes.name: Park in Mestre + train to Santa Lucia
modes.notes: Valid if Peschiera parking were full, which is the backup, not the plan. Extra drive past the family's natural station.

modes.name: Bardolino car → Peschiera station → train → Venezia S. Lucia
modes.cost_eur: Peschiera station parking ~€1.50/h or ~€15/day; regional seats from ~€11–15 adult; high-speed more
modes.notes: Drive 14 km / ~20 minutes via SR249. Park at Piazzale Stazione (24/7). Direct trains typically 1h28. Arrive in Venice, not at a garage. This is the winner.

modes.name: Organized bus/boat day tour from Lake Garda
modes.notes: You cannot leave when the baby melts down. Many itineraries advertise Venice + shopping stops and return early evening.

day_plan.target_train_window: 07:50–08:20 (verify Trenitalia the night before; prefer a direct train ~1h28)
loop: Arrive Santa Lucia. Change nappy in station toilets. Carrier on. Stroller folded.

Optional: ACTV vaporetto Line 1 one stop-rich ride down the Grand Canal as a seated rest — buy singles unless you will ride twice (24h cards are usually waste on this short plan). Skip if the boat looks crushed; walk Lista di Spagna instead.
Rialto campo: coffee, shade, watch boats. Do not climb the Rialto steps with a fully loaded stroller.
Early lunch away from the bridge crush (San Polo side or Strada Nova cafes with indoor seats).
One extra campo only if the baby is actually asleep or content. Not San Marco and not Burano.
Back to Santa Lucia with 20 minutes platform buffer.
skip: Anything that requires a timed entry after 14:00

stroller_protocol.primary: Soft structured carrier. Venice is not stroller-friendly: 400+ stepped bridges.
stroller_protocol.secondary: Compact stroller for Peschiera platform, Santa Lucia concourse, and emergency nap if you find a long flat fondamenta.
stroller_protocol.vaporetto: Fold. Gaps and crowds. Carrier is safer at the boarding edge.
stroller_protocol.do_not: Do not attempt a full San Marco circuit with a full-size stroller.

costs_eur.infant_train: Usually free on regional; check high-speed occupancy rules

rainy_variant.summary: Train plan still wins in rain — more indoor stretches at the station and cafes. Shorten the outdoor loop. Buy the earlier return. Do not 'add a museum marathon' that overruns 15:20.
indoor_ideas: A short bookshop or supermarket run for supplies
Skip vaporetto if decks are wet and crowded

verify_night_before: Trenitalia or Trenord app: pick a direct Peschiera → Venezia S. Lucia and the return that lands you on a train departing Venice by 15:20.
Peschiera station parking occupancy is rarely bookable — have Mestre as a nuclear backup only.
ACTV vaporetto prices if you still want Line 1.
